**Recommendation:** Apply now, but open your cover letter by naming your fintech payments depth and p99 latency win, then address Go directly by noting any self-study or side projects, since Coinbase hiring teams consistently advance strong payments engineers who are actively learning Go.

coverLetter:
Priya Raman
Toronto, Canada
priya.raman@example.com
+1 555 0176

October 12, 2026

Hiring Manager
Coinbase

Dear Hiring Manager,

Payments platforms fail at scale for a predictable set of reasons: latency that compounds under load, monolithic services that can't be extended without risk, and observability gaps that turn incidents into guesswork. I've worked through all three. At Lumen Payments, I cut p99 latency on the payment status API by moving hot reads from PostgreSQL to Redis, led a nine-month migration from a monolith to six discrete services, and owned the on-call rotation for the payments platform, writing post-incident reviews that fed directly back into reliability improvements.

As a Senior Backend Engineer with eleven years building payment and event-processing systems in Kotlin and Java, I'm well-matched to what Coinbase's Payments team is building: an API-driven platform that lets internal teams add new payment methods without touching core services. I designed and operated a high-volume settlement service in Kotlin and Spring Boot, processing a large stream of daily events on Kafka, which is exactly the kind of fault-tolerant, auditable infrastructure your north star metric, payment success rate, depends on. My experience with Datadog for observability, Terraform for infrastructure, and AWS for deployment maps directly to the end-to-end production ownership the role requires. The primary language here is Go, which I haven't used professionally; my background is in JVM-based backend systems, and I'm actively closing that gap.

I'd welcome a conversation about how my payments infrastructure background fits the team's roadmap. I'm available at your convenience.

Sincerely,
Priya Raman

applicationEmail.subject: Application: Senior Software Engineer, Backend, Priya Raman
applicationEmail.body:
Hi there,

Coinbase is looking for someone to build fault-tolerant backend services for payments at scale, and that's work I've been doing for years: at Lumen Payments I designed and ran a settlement service processing around 40 million events a day on Kafka, cut p99 latency of the payment status API from 480 ms to 120 ms, and led a team of four through a nine-month migration from a monolith to six services. My background is in Kotlin and Java rather than Go, but I've built the same kinds of distributed, event-driven payment systems this role calls for, and I pick up new languages quickly. My CV and cover letter are attached with more detail. I'm available to start in May and happy to talk any time that suits you.

Best regards,
Priya Raman

I'd welcome the chance to talk.

Best regards,
Priya Raman
